stubs.angle: With Logging:LogLevel:Default set to Warning in appsettings.json, which of LogDebug, LogInformation, LogWarning and LogError calls reach the console provider?
stubs.answerHinge: The configured level is a minimum: only entries at Warning or above (Warning, Error, Critical) are written, and Information and Debug are discarded.

stubs.angle: A BCL snippet records request duration into a Histogram<double> from a TimeSpan and prints the recorded value; for a 2.5 second request it prints 500 instead of 2500, so find the defective line.
stubs.answerHinge: TimeSpan.Milliseconds is only the 0-999 millisecond component, so durations of a second or more wrap; TotalMilliseconds (or TotalSeconds) must be recorded.

stubs.angle: Which statement correctly describes what a feature flag (release toggle) changes about shipping unfinished functionality to production?
stubs.answerHinge: A release toggle decouples deployment from release: the code is deployed dark and switched on for users later without a new deployment, at the cost of flag debt that must be removed.

stubs.angle: Which cache key should a CI job use for the NuGet packages folder of a .NET solution so the cache is reused but never serves stale dependencies?
stubs.answerHinge: The key must be derived from a hash of the dependency manifest (packages.lock.json files) so it changes exactly when dependencies change, not from the commit SHA or a fixed string.

stubs.angle: Select the true statements about Counter, UpDownCounter and the observable instruments in System.Diagnostics.Metrics.
stubs.answerHinge: A Counter only increases and fits totals such as handled requests, an UpDownCounter can also decrease and fits values such as items in a queue, and observable instruments report through a callback that runs only when a listener collects, not on every change.

stubs.angle: Select the true statements about ILogger.BeginScope with a state such as a dictionary holding OrderId.
stubs.answerHinge: Scope properties are attached to every entry logged inside the using block, including after await because scopes flow with the async context, but only providers that support scopes (for example console with IncludeScopes) emit them.

stubs.angle: Which checks should the CI pipeline of a .NET service run on every pull request, in what order, and why?
stubs.answerHinge: Cheap, fast checks run first to fail fast (restore in locked mode, format verification, build with warnings as errors), then tests, then publish of one artifact, and the pull request merges only when the pipeline is green.

stubs.angle: With an ActivityListener registered, a snippet starts an Import activity without disposing it and then a Health activity that should be a root, but the program prints Import as the parent, so find the defective line.
stubs.answerHinge: StartActivity sets Activity.Current, and an activity that is never stopped or disposed stays current, so every later activity in that async context becomes its child; the fix is a using declaration.

stubs.angle: Why does a hot-path call _logger.LogDebug("Item {Id} at {Price}", id, price) with int and decimal arguments still allocate when Debug is disabled, and what removes the cost?
stubs.answerHinge: The LoggerExtensions methods take params object[], so the array and the boxed value types are created at the call site before the level check; a [LoggerMessage] generated method or an IsEnabled guard avoids it.

stubs.angle: Select the true statements about W3C baggage carried with OpenTelemetry in .NET services.
stubs.answerHinge: Baggage travels in a plain HTTP header to every downstream service, including third parties, it is not added to span attributes automatically, and it is subject to size limits, so it must never carry secrets or personal data.

stubs.angle: A service has a 99.9% availability SLO over 30 days: how do you build alerts on it with error-budget burn rate instead of a fixed error-rate threshold?
stubs.answerHinge: Burn rate is the observed error ratio divided by the allowed ratio (1 - SLO), and paging on a high burn rate over both a long and a short window catches fast budget loss quickly while ignoring brief blips.

stubs.angle: How do you keep one distributed trace when an ASP.NET Core API publishes a message that a separate worker consumes, and how do you model a consumer that processes a batch of messages?
stubs.answerHinge: HTTP propagation does not cover the broker, so the producer must inject traceparent into message headers and the consumer must extract it to start its span, using span links instead of a single parent when one span handles messages from many traces.

stubs.angle: After a release the logging bill triples because one service writes millions of Information entries per minute; what do you do right now and afterwards?
stubs.answerHinge: Find the noisy category first, then raise its minimum level through a per-category filter in reloadable configuration so the change applies without a redeploy, and afterwards fix the log statement and add volume alerts and review rules.

stubs.angle: Your team releases once a month on Friday evening with a long manual checklist, and most releases need a hotfix; as tech lead, how do you change this?
stubs.answerHinge: Large infrequent batches are the cause of risk, so the plan is to shrink batch size and release more often through pipeline automation, measured with lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate and time to restore, rolled out step by step with the team.

stubs.angle: The on-call engineer receives about 200 alerts a week, most are ignored, and a real outage was missed; what do you do as tech lead?
stubs.answerHinge: A page must be urgent, actionable and tied to user-facing symptoms, so the lead runs an alert review with owners that deletes alerts or downgrades them to tickets and makes alert quality a recurring part of the on-call process.

stubs.angle: Management wants every production deployment approved by a weekly change advisory board; how do you argue for a different approval model, and what do you propose?
stubs.answerHinge: External heavyweight approval slows delivery without lowering the change failure rate, so peer review plus automated pipeline gates with an audit trail give the same control at lower cost and risk.

stubs.angle: How do you design the rollout of code and configuration changes for a platform that runs in many regions, so that one bad change cannot cause a global outage?
stubs.answerHinge: Changes, including configuration, go through progressive exposure in rings (internal, a small region, then the rest) with bake time, health gates that halt the rollout automatically, and a fast rollback path, trading release speed for a bounded blast radius.
